PF<sub>5</sub>

en.explanation:
Hybridization (X) = [ VE + MA – c + a ]

where, VE = No. of valence electrons of central atom
MA = No. of monovalent atoms/groups surrounding the central atom,
c = Charge on the cation,
a = Charge on the anion

(A) [BrF5] : X = [ 7 + 5 - 0 + 0] = 6 = sp3d2 hybridized

(B) [SF6] : X = [ 6 + 6 - 0 + 0] = 6 = sp3d2 hybridized

(C) [CrF6]3 : Cr+3 = [Ar]3d3

(D) [PF5] : X = [ 5 + 5 - 0 + 0] = 5 = sp3d hybridized

Note : [CrF6]3 shows d2sp3 hybridization not sp3d2. So option (C) should also be the correct answer.

en.content: Additin of sodium hydroxide solution to a weak acid (HA)results in a buffer of pH 6. If ionition constant of HA is 10<sup><mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.186ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.76ex" height="1.505ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -583 778 665" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mo"><use data-c="2212" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>5</sup>, the ratio of salt to acid concentration in the buffer solution will be :
en.explanation:
HA      H+ + A

Ka = = 105

pH = pKa + log

6 = log [105] + log

6 = 5 + log

log = 1

= 10

Salt : Acid = 10 : 1
